I queued the task "Add CSV export to the customers page" to run now. Nothing built yet. No thread has reported back.

Brief asks for:
- **Export:** an "Export CSV" link on `/customers` that downloads all customers as `customers.csv`.
- **Columns:** Name, VAT, Created, with dates as DD/MM/YYYY.
- **Safety:** commas, quotes and line breaks in names are handled. Cells starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` are neutralised so spreadsheets don't run them as formulas.
- **Checks:** unit tests, browser test, CHANGELOG entry, and lint, tests and changelog check all passing.
- **Proof:** thread must start the app, click Export CSV itself, and send back a working browser link plus the CSV content it got. Work ends in a pull request.

Notebook updated with the plan.

{"title":"Add CSV export to the customers page","brief":"Owner request: "Add a CSV export to the customers page".

Requested result: the owner wants this built. Done means a user on /customers can click a visible "Export CSV" link/button and download a CSV of all customers, working end to end in the running app.

Context:
- Node 20 + TypeScript app. src/customers/index.ts stores customers (id, name, vat, createdAt ISO string) in $SANDBOX_DATA_DIR/customers.json. src/web/server.ts is a plain node:http server rendering the /customers page (table with Name and VAT columns) and /api/customers (JSON).
- Scripts: npm start, npm test (vitest), npm run test:browser (playwright, tests/browser/customers.spec.ts), npm run lint (tsc --noEmit), npm run check:changelog.
- Project convention: dates shown to users are always DD/MM/YYYY.

What to build:
- A route such as GET /customers.csv (or /api/customers.csv) returning text/csv; charset=utf-8 with Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="customers.csv". Make sure the existing `/customers` prefix match in server.ts does not swallow the new route.
- Columns: Name, VAT, Created (DD/MM/YYYY). Header row always present, even with zero customers.
- Correct CSV escaping per RFC 4180: quote fields containing comma, quote, CR or LF; double embedded quotes. Use CRLF line endings. Guard against spreadsheet formula injection (prefix cells starting with =, +, -, @ with a single quote or equivalent).
- Put the CSV serialisation in a small pure, unit-tested function (not inline in the server).
- Add an "Export CSV" link on the customers page near the heading/table, styled consistently with the existing page. No emoji.

Tests:
- Unit tests for the CSV function: empty list, escaping of commas/quotes/newlines, formula-injection guard, date format.
- Extend tests/browser/customers.spec.ts: link visible on /customers, and the download (or response) has the right headers and content.
- npm test, npm run lint, npm run test:browser and npm run check:changelog must all pass. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry.

Verification for the report: start the app as a managed app (jevellan_app_start) with some seeded customers, open /customers in a browser, click Export CSV, confirm the downloaded file content, and return the verified browser link plus the CSV content you saw.
